title: Raspberry-Glazed Laminated Cronut-Style Doughnuts
summary: Buttery laminated yeast-dough rings fried into tall, flaky layers and dipped in pink raspberry glaze.
equipment: 8 cm round cutter and 2.5 cm round cutter
baking trays lined with lightly floured baking paper
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt in the mixer bowl, then add the cold milk, water, egg and soft butter. Knead on low for 4 min to a smooth, fairly firm dough. Press it into a 15 cm square, wrap and chill for 1 h.

steps.title: Prepare the butter
steps.text: Lay the cold butter between two sheets of baking paper, beat it flat with the rolling pin and roll it into a 14 cm square. Chill for 15 min; it should be cold but bend without snapping.

steps.title: Lock in the butter
steps.text: Roll the dough into a 22 cm square, place the butter on top turned like a diamond and fold the four corners of dough over it to meet in the centre. Pinch the seams so the butter is sealed in.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Roll the parcel into a 45 x 20 cm strip, fold it in three like a letter, wrap and chill for 30 min. Do this twice more, turning the dough a quarter turn each time, then chill for 1 h.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Roll the dough 1.8 cm thick, about 24 cm square, and cut 8 cm rounds with a 2.5 cm hole in each to make 9. Space them well apart on the floured trays.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover loosely and leave somewhere cool, no warmer than 25 °C, for 1.5-2 h, until puffy and the layers start to open at the sides.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Fill the pan with oil to about 4 cm, no more than half full, and heat it to 175 °C.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Fry 2-3 rings at a time for 2-3 min a side at 170-175 °C, until deep golden and risen into tall layers. The centre should read about 90 °C on a probe, with no doughy streak between the layers. Drain on the rack and cool completely.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Push the raspberries through the sieve to get about 30 ml of juice. Whisk it with the icing sugar and lemon juice to a thick pink glaze, adding a few drops of water if needed. Dip the top of each ring and leave for 15 min to set.

tips: The most common mistake is letting the butter get warm; if it oozes or the dough feels greasy, chill for 20 min before carrying on.
Prove somewhere cool; above 25 °C the butter melts out and the layers vanish.
Use a sharp cutter and press straight down without twisting so the layers rise evenly.
Fry one test ring first and cut it open to check the inside is cooked.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep uncovered at room temperature for a few hours; they soften in a box.
